title: Historical Left and Right Abutment Seepage Summary, 1969–2020
description: Annual maximum seepage at left and right abutment drainage weirs correlated with concurrent reservoir elevation at time of maximum reading. Left abutment Weir 1 measures combined abutment and arch gallery drainage through 2001; Weir 2 (arch gallery only) installed 1995. Right abutment Weir 3 installed 2001. Values reported at near-normal pool conditions.
units: seepage in gpm; reservoir elevation in ft-MSL
source: EBID Weir Records 1969–2020; CDSC FERC Part 12D Inspection Report, October 2020, Table 3-1

rows: First full operational season; baseline established

title: Right Abutment Crest Displacement Monitoring, 1995–2025
description: Annual survey monument readings for right abutment crest monuments RA-1 through RA-4. Positive values indicate downstream displacement from 1995 baseline (zero). RA-1 is on the powerhouse structure (concrete/rock); RA-2 through RA-4 are on the embankment crest at increasing distances from the arch contact. Average is mean of RA-2 through RA-4. Rate is 5-year rolling average displacement rate.
units: displacement in inches (positive = downstream); rate in inches per year
source: EBID Annual Survey Records 1995–2025; EBID Instrumentation and Monitoring Summary 2015–2025, October 2025, Table 2

units: elevations in ft-MSL; depths in ft below ground surface
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 1

title: Embankment Clay Core Index Properties — Boring B-1
description: Index property test results on undisturbed Shelby tube samples and disturbed jar samples from the embankment clay core (Zone 2) intercepted in boring B-1. All tests per ASTM D4318 (Atterberg limits) and ASTM D698/D1557 (Proctor). Relative compaction based on modified Proctor (ASTM D1557) maximum dry density of 106.9 pcf.
units: depths in ft below gallery floor; MC and LL/PL/PI in percent; density in pcf
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 4

title: Glacial Till Index Properties — Right Abutment Boring B-4
description: Index properties for glacial till (basal till, GC) samples from boring B-4 on the right abutment. Samples obtained by Shelby tube push (ST) and split-spoon (SS) at depths producing best recovery in the fine-matrix-rich intervals. Gradation by ASTM D422.
notes: SPT refusal (N > 50) at 50 ft and 65 ft depth; till classified as very dense. Gravel fraction includes particles 4.75 mm to 75 mm; larger cobbles excluded from gradation sample. Both samples classified as GC (clayey gravel) per USCS — matrix-supported fabric governs engineering behavior.
units: depths in ft below ground surface; percentages by weight
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 5

title: Consolidated-Undrained Triaxial Test Results (ASTM D4767)
description: CU triaxial shear tests with pore pressure measurement on embankment clay core and glacial till specimens. Specimens prepared from undisturbed Shelby tube samples. Confining pressures span the in-situ stress range. Effective stress failure envelopes are Mohr-Coulomb linear fits to the test data.
notes: Failure defined at maximum deviator stress (peak strength). Linear Mohr-Coulomb envelopes fitted to paired test results for clay core (specimens 1a and 1b). Single till specimen; φ' reported with c' = 0 for conservative long-term analysis (actual test shows minor c' ≈ 50 psf, neglected). Strain at failure: clay core 4.2–5.8%, glacial till 8.1%.
units: stresses in psf; friction angle in degrees
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 6

title: Fresh Granodiorite Unconfined Compressive Strength (ASTM D7012 Method C)
description: UCS test results on NX cores from fresh granodiorite (ISRM Grade I–II) recovered from borings B-1 through B-4 below the weathering front. Specimens prepared per ASTM D7012; length-to-diameter ratio maintained at 2.0–2.5:1. E50 is the secant modulus at 50% of peak stress. Failure modes: S = shear plane, S-E = shear + extension, C = cone/triaxial.
units: depth in ft below ground surface; dimensions in inches; UCS in psi; E50 in 10⁶ psi
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 7

title: Weathered Granodiorite Unconfined Compressive Strength
description: UCS test results on specimens from the highly weathered granodiorite zone (ISRM Grades IV–V) above the weathering front in left abutment borings. High variability reflects heterogeneous weathering. Some specimens are hand-trimmed due to poor core quality; these are flagged. ISRM weathering grade per ISRM (1981) classification scheme.

summary_statistics.note: High variability (COV = 44%) is typical for weathered rock; use lower-bound values for conservative foundation design

units: depth in ft below ground surface (gallery floor collar); UCS in psi
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 8

rows: Hand-trimmed; friable; lowest strength in program

title: Fresh Granodiorite Indirect Tensile Strength — Brazilian Disk Test (ASTM D3967)
description: Brazilian disk indirect tensile strength (ITS) test results on NX-diameter disks from fresh granodiorite. Disk thickness t approximately equal to half the diameter (D/2). Load applied diametrically per ASTM D3967. Failure mode: C = central splitting (valid), I = irregular (excluded from statistics).

summary_statistics.note: UCS/ITS ratio of 11.2 is consistent with intact, low-microcrack rock (typical range 8–14 for granitic rock)

units: depth in ft; diameter and thickness in inches; peak load in lbf; ITS in psi
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 9

title: Concrete Core Compressive Strength by ASR Severity Zone (ASTM C42 / ASTM C39)
description: Compressive strength test results on NX-diameter concrete cores from the arch crown section. Cores drilled vertically from dam crest November 2025. Depth measured from downstream face. ASR severity zone assigned by petrographic analysis (ASTM C856).
units: depth in ft from downstream face; f'c in psi
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 10

rows: Active gel exudation on ends; map cracking visible
Gel in aggregate cracks; pervasive microcracking
Moderate gel; some aggregate particles intact
Gel in aggregate interfaces; minor microcracking
No gel; intact paste; excellent aggregate bond

title: Concrete Core Split Tensile (Indirect Tensile) Strength by ASR Zone (ASTM C496)
description: Split cylinder indirect tensile strength test results on NX-diameter concrete core specimens from the arch crown. Specimens prepared from the same core holes as the compressive strength tests (Table 10). ITS formula: f't = 2P / (π × d × L). ASR zones confirmed by petrographic analysis.

zone_summary.Zone_1_note: Range from multiple petrographic specimens: 295–345 psi; mean 320 psi (this specimen is near lower bound)

units: depth in ft from downstream face; dimensions in inches; load in lbf; f't in psi
source: MWDE PFR Geotechnical Investigation Report, November 2025, Table 11

title: Annual Seepage Summary 2015–2025
description: Annual maximum seepage readings for all active weirs and drainage collection points, measured at or near normal pool conditions. Weir 1 = left abutment foundation gallery; Weir 2 = arch gallery (installed 1995); Weir 3 = right abutment toe drain (installed 2001). Left Total = Weir 1 + Weir 2; Dam Total = Left Total + Right Total + Arch Gallery. Reservoir elevation is concurrent reading at time of maximum seepage.

trend_summary.arch_gallery_trend: Slight increase 1.2 to 1.8 gpm (50% increase over decade)

units: seepage in gpm; reservoir elevation in ft-MSL
source: EBID Instrumentation and Monitoring Summary 2015–2025, October 2025, Table 12

title: Piezometer P-3 Historical Readings 2010–2025 (Left Abutment Weathered Granodiorite)
description: Historical readings from piezometer P-3, installed in 1988 in the left abutment at elevation 4,168 ft-MSL, within the highly weathered granodiorite zone 50 ft below the embankment crest. P-3 was converted from an open standpipe to a vibrating wire instrument in 2003. Readings are near-simultaneous with Weir 1 seepage readings. Reservoir elevation is concurrent reading.

trend_summary.correlation_with_seepage: Strong positive correlation (r = 0.97 over 6 readings); both seepage and P-3 increasing at consistent rates

units: pore pressure in psi; equivalent head in ft of water; reservoir elevation in ft-MSL
source: EBID Instrumentation and Monitoring Summary 2015–2025, October 2025, Table 13; CDSC Part 12D Inspection Report 2020 for pre-2015 values

rows: Baseline reading; VW instrument stable post-2003 conversion
Most recent; 71% increase from 2010 baseline over 15 years

title: Remediation Cost Summary — Elk Basin Dam
description: Opinion of probable cost for recommended and contingency remediation alternatives evaluated in the November 2025 MWDE Remediation Alternatives Evaluation. Costs are in 2025 USD. Ranges reflect uncertainty in subsurface conditions and contractor pricing; lower bound assumes favorable conditions and competitive bidding, upper bound reflects adverse conditions. Priority: 1 = highest urgency.
units: costs in 2025 US dollars; all items include engineering, construction, and inspection unless noted
source: MWDE Remediation Alternatives Evaluation, November 2025, Table 5-1
